STEP 1 - Scene: Breakfast-style snack: two slices of toasted bread on a white paper plate, with a cup of coffee or tea and two jam packets (strawberry). Photographed from a fairly high, near-overhead angle on a tray, with a color calibration card and a label "3036" in view.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The white paper plate is roughly 17 cm in diameter (small side plate scale). Area = 3.14 x (8.5)^2 ≈ 227 cm^2. The tray is about 35 cm wide, consistent with this sizing.

STEP 3 - Items: (1) toasted white/wheat bread, two slices; (2) strawberry jam, two packets (~15 g each); (3) black coffee or tea in a cup (liquid, not counted as a food item in the plate estimate, but included for energy as black coffee is near zero kcal).

STEP 4 - Area: Two toast slices together cover about 45% of the plate area (each slice ~50 cm^2 visible, overlapping partly off the plate edge; estimate ~100 cm^2 total of plate area, roughly 45%). Jam packets sit beside the plate on the tray, not on the plate.

STEP 5 - Volume: Toast slices are thin. Two slices ~ 2 x (about 12 x 11 cm x 1.2 cm) ≈ 2 x 158 ml... more accurately each slice is about 80 cm^2 x 1.2 cm ≈ 96 ml, so ~190 ml total gross for toast before density correction.

STEP 6 - Grams: Bread-like slices at ~0.3 g/ml (bread loaf density, since toast is airy) gives ≈ 57 g of toast. Each jam packet is about 15 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Toast (wheat/white bread, toasted) ≈ 270 kcal/100 g → 57 g ≈ 154 kcal. Strawberry jam ≈ 250 kcal/100 g → 30 g (two packets) ≈ 75 kcal. Black coffee/tea ≈ 2 kcal (negligible, with cup of liquid taken as ~0 kcal).

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Two slices of toast weighing about 57 g total is plausible for thin slices (typical slice ~30 g, but these look thin and partially toasted). Total ~87 g of food, ~230 kcal, plausible for a light breakfast snack with jam.
